correctness.rationale: The local update is reconstructed for each degree r+2, including tie retention. A finite symmetric-weight Lyapunov identity proves eventual periods at most two. Periodic private-leaf uniformity gives a bijection with ordered binary phase words. For r=1, the double cover is one 2n-cycle when n odd and two n-cycles when even; its exact four-state determinant gives Q_j. For r=2, both forward and backward flip conditions give an explicit 16-state transfer and its exact characteristic polynomial. For r>=3, three identical leaves strictly dominate two cycle neighbours after one step, giving F^3=F on all initial configurations. The embedded verifier checks the algebra and 751424 individually labelled states; these finite checks are corroboration, not proof of unbounded n.

originality.rationale: The specified contribution is the three-regime exact fixed- and primitive-two-cycle census on unicyclic coronas with r private leaves at each site; the Fibonacci/Lucas fixed count on a single ring and the general period-two theorem are prior results, not novel claims. The fully inspected 1988 cyclic-majority article does not add leaf delays or count their recurrent two-cycles. The 2014 complete preprint supplies a general convergence framework but no fixed graph-family exact census; the 2022 tree article treats a distinct tree domain. Accessible historical claims on XOR sunlets and majority prisms do not imply these majority-corona formulas. A search cannot certify historical uniqueness; unindexed equivalent classifications remain a bounded residual risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier majority-with-delayed-input or graph-corona transfer-matrix results may reproduce the private-leaf trichotomy.
The full text of Lemoy–Mozeika–Seki (2014) was not inspected; the abstract indicates a different noisy automaton, but does not prove absence of a related limiting calculation.
Only general convergence theorem, not its original 1980 full article, was directly rechecked; correctness of the present bound does not depend on that text.

value.rationale: The object is a natural one-parameter sequence of cycle coronas modeling one, two, or many private followers of each cycle site. Their nonlinear synchronous majority dynamics has a nontrivial exact attractor phase diagram with exponential recurrent counts 2.618^n, 3.249^n, and 4^n. The r=1 double-cover parity split, r=2 new transfer quartic and r>=3 one-step periodicity together form a complete natural infinite-family classification, rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a known fixed-point table. The previously known ring Q_n component is expressly excluded from novelty.
